duplicate_policy.method: Each quiz draw avoids repeated question IDs in the same quiz and avoids recently shown IDs stored in the browser when enough unused questions are available.

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: River Junior High School opened a new reading corner beside the school library. At first, some students thought it was just another quiet space. However, the reading corner soon became popular because students could borrow short books, magazines, and English comics during lunch break. The English teacher, Ms. Lin, also placed a suggestion box there. Students could write down topics they wanted to read about. After two weeks, the most popular topics were sports, animals, and travel. Ms. Lin said the reading corner was not only for strong readers. It was for anyone who wanted to build a small reading habit.

passages.label: Passage B
passages.text: Notice: The reading corner is open from 12:10 to 12:50 on school days. Students may borrow one book at a time and return it within seven days.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Passage A?
options: A school opened a reading space to encourage students to read.
A teacher closed the school library during lunch.
A class went on a trip to a library.
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on the new reading corner and how it encourages reading.

questions.question: Where is the new reading corner?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says it opened beside the school library.

questions.question: Why did Ms. Lin place a suggestion box in the reading corner?
options: To learn what students wanted to read.
To collect money for new desks.
To choose students for a contest.
To stop students from borrowing books.
questions.explanation: Students wrote down reading topics they wanted, so the box helped the teacher understand their interests.

questions.question: What does "popular" most likely mean in Passage A?
questions.explanation: Many students used the reading corner, so it became liked by many people.

questions.question: What does "there" refer to in "placed a suggestion box there"?
questions.explanation: "There" refers to the reading corner.

questions.question: What does Ms. Lin mean by saying the corner is for anyone who wants to build a small reading habit?
options: Students do not need to be excellent readers to use it.
Only strong readers can borrow books.
Students must read long books every day.
The reading corner is only for teachers.
questions.explanation: The sentence means the corner welcomes all students who want to read more.

questions.question: According to both passages, which statement is true?
options: Students can use the reading corner during lunch break.
Students can borrow three books at a time.
The reading corner is open after school only.
Students must return books on the same day.
questions.explanation: Passage A mentions lunch break, and Passage B gives the lunch-time opening hours.

questions.question: Which topic was one of the most popular topics in the suggestion box? Brief answer: Why might this help Ms. Lin choose books?
questions.sample_brief_answer: It helps Ms. Lin choose books that students are interested in.
questions.explanation: Animals was one of the three popular topics.

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: Nora planned to visit her cousin on Sunday afternoon. She usually took Bus 16 because it stopped near her cousin's apartment. This Sunday, however, the city changed the bus schedule because of a road race. Nora checked the notice at the bus stop before leaving home. She learned that Bus 16 would not stop at Garden Road between 1:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. Her cousin told her to take Bus 22 instead and get off at Lake Street. Nora left earlier than usual because she did not want to be late.

passages.label: Chart
passages.text: Bus 16: no Garden Road stop from 1:00-4:00 p.m.; Bus 22: stops at Lake Street every 20 minutes; Bus 30: stops at City Hall only.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Nora needed to change her travel plan because of a bus schedule change.
Nora joined a road race on Sunday.
Nora moved to a new apartment.
Nora learned how to drive a bus.
questions.explanation: The passage is about Nora changing her bus plan.

questions.question: Which bus did Nora usually take?
questions.explanation: The passage says she usually took Bus 16.

questions.question: According to the chart, which bus stops at Lake Street?
questions.explanation: The chart says Bus 22 stops at Lake Street every 20 minutes.

questions.question: Why did Nora leave earlier than usual?
options: She wanted to avoid being late.
She wanted to watch the road race.
She had to buy a new phone.
questions.explanation: The last sentence states her reason.

questions.question: What does "instead" mean in the passage?
questions.explanation: Her cousin suggested Bus 22 as another choice.

questions.question: What does "it" refer to in "because it stopped near her cousin's apartment"?
questions.explanation: "It" refers to Bus 16.

questions.question: What does the sentence "the city changed the bus schedule because of a road race" mean?
options: The bus times and stops were different because a race was happening.
The city bought new buses for students.
The road race was canceled by the city.
questions.explanation: The schedule changed due to the road race.

questions.question: Which bus should Nora take to visit her cousin during the road race? Brief answer: Give one reason.
questions.sample_brief_answer: She should take Bus 22 because Bus 16 will not stop at Garden Road during that time.
questions.explanation: Bus 22 is the alternative suggested by her cousin.

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: The student council at East High School wanted to improve school lunches. Before making suggestions to the cafeteria, they asked 120 students about their favorite lunch choices. The survey showed that rice boxes were still the most popular, but many students also wanted more fruit and soup. Some students said the food was fine, but the lines were too long. After reading the results, the student council decided to make two suggestions: add one fruit option every day and open a second line for students who only wanted soup or drinks.

passages.label: Chart
passages.text: Favorite lunch choices: rice box 48 students; noodles 30 students; sandwich 22 students; salad 12 students; soup only 8 students.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the survey?
options: To choose a new school principal.
questions.explanation: The council wanted to improve school lunches.

questions.question: How many students joined the survey?
questions.explanation: The passage says 120 students were asked.

questions.question: Which lunch choice was the most popular?
questions.explanation: The chart shows rice box had 48 students, the highest number.

questions.question: Why did the council suggest opening a second line?
options: To stop students from buying soup.
questions.explanation: Some students said the lines were too long.

questions.question: What does "suggestions" most likely mean?
options: ideas offered for people to consider
questions.explanation: The council made ideas for the cafeteria to consider.

questions.question: What does "they" refer to in "they asked 120 students"?
questions.explanation: "They" refers to the student council.

questions.question: According to the passage and chart, which statement is true?
options: More students chose noodles than sandwiches.
Soup only was the most popular choice.
Rice boxes were less popular than sandwiches.
questions.explanation: Noodles had 30 students, and sandwiches had 22.

questions.question: Which suggestion is directly connected to students wanting more healthy options? Brief answer: Explain your choice.
options: Add one fruit option every day.
questions.sample_brief_answer: Fruit is a healthy option, and many students wanted more fruit.
questions.explanation: The passage connects students' request for fruit with the council's suggestion.

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: The City Science Museum is holding a special exhibition about light and color. Visitors can learn why the sky looks blue, how rainbows form, and how artists use color to create different feelings. The exhibition is designed for families and students. It includes short videos, simple experiments, and a small drawing area. The museum hopes visitors will not only read about science but also touch, test, and create.

passages.label: Passage B
passages.text: Museum Message: Student groups of 10 or more should book tickets at least three days before their visit. The exhibition is closed on Mondays. Photos are allowed, but flash photography is not.

questions.question: What is the exhibition mainly about?
questions.explanation: The first sentence states the topic.

questions.question: Which activity is included in the exhibition?
questions.explanation: The passage lists simple experiments as part of the exhibition.

questions.question: Why does the museum include videos, experiments, and a drawing area?
options: To stop students from asking questions.
questions.explanation: The museum wants visitors to touch, test, and create.

questions.question: What does "designed for" most likely mean?
questions.explanation: The exhibition is made for families and students.

questions.question: What does "It" refer to in "It includes short videos"?
questions.explanation: "It" refers to the exhibition.

questions.question: What does "touch, test, and create" suggest about the exhibition?
options: Visitors can learn by doing things.
Visitors must stay quiet all the time.
questions.explanation: The phrase suggests hands-on learning.

questions.question: A class of 12 students wants to visit on Monday. What problem do they have?
options: The exhibition is closed on Mondays.
Student groups cannot visit the museum.
The exhibition has no science activities.
questions.explanation: Passage B says the exhibition is closed on Mondays.

questions.question: Which rule should a student group remember? Brief answer: Why is this rule important for planning?
options: Book tickets at least three days before the visit.
Use flash photography in every room.
questions.sample_brief_answer: They need to book early, so the museum can prepare for the group.
questions.explanation: The message clearly states the booking rule.

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: The school volleyball team lost its first game of the season. After the game, Coach Wang did not blame the players. Instead, he asked them to watch a video of the match and write down one thing they did well and one thing they needed to improve. Most players noticed that they missed many serves in the second half. The team decided to add a short serving practice before every regular practice. Three weeks later, the players felt more confident. They still made mistakes, but they were no longer afraid of serving during important points.

passages.label: Schedule
passages.text: Tuesday: serving practice 4:00-4:20, team practice 4:20-5:30. Thursday: serving practice 4:00-4:20, team practice 4:20-5:30. Saturday: practice game 9:00-10:30.

questions.question: What is Passage A mainly about?
options: A team improved by finding a problem and practicing it.
A coach stopped all team practices.
A school canceled its volleyball season.
Players learned a new school song.
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on improving serving through practice.

questions.question: What did Coach Wang ask players to do after the game?
options: Watch a video and write down strengths and weaknesses.
Run around the school ten times.
questions.explanation: The passage states this directly.

questions.question: What kind of coach is Coach Wang probably?
options: A coach who helps players learn from mistakes.
A coach who never watches games.
A coach who blames players first.
A coach who dislikes practice plans.
questions.explanation: He asked players to review and improve instead of blaming them.

questions.question: What does "confident" most likely mean?
questions.explanation: The players became less afraid of serving.

questions.question: What does "they" refer to in "they were no longer afraid"?
questions.explanation: "They" refers to the players.

questions.question: What does "he did not blame the players" mean?
options: He did not say the loss was only their fault.
He asked them to leave the team.
questions.explanation: Not blaming means he did not simply say the players were at fault.

questions.question: According to the schedule, how long is serving practice on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: Serving practice is from 4:00 to 4:20.

questions.question: Which practice was added to help the team improve? Brief answer: Why did they add it?
questions.sample_brief_answer: They added serving practice because many players missed serves in the second half.
questions.explanation: The team found serving was a weakness.

questions.question: Put the events in the correct order.
options: The team lost its first game. → Players watched the video. → The team added serving practice. → Players felt more confident.
Players felt more confident. → The team lost its first game. → Players watched the video. → The team added serving practice.
The team added serving practice. → The team lost its first game. → Players felt more confident. → Players watched the video.
Players watched the video. → Players felt more confident. → The team lost its first game. → The team added serving practice.
questions.explanation: The passage first describes the lost game, then the video review, then extra serving practice, and finally the team's greater confidence.

items.title: Storm Notes for June
items.topic: 天氣、公共安全、圖表閱讀
items.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center Atlantic Hurricane Outlook; https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/outlooks/hurricane.shtml?vm=r; accessed 2026-06-01
items.usage: 依 NOAA 2026 大西洋颶風季展望重寫短文與圖表，用於題材與數字查證，未直接複製原文。

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: At school, Kevin helped the science club make a June safety poster. He read NOAA's outlook for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season and learned that a below-normal season was the most likely result. Still, his teacher reminded everyone that below-normal does not mean danger-free. A single strong storm can still cause serious flooding, power cuts, and travel problems. Kevin added three simple tips to the poster: check weather updates, prepare flashlights and water, and talk with family members about where to go in an emergency. He also wrote that the Atlantic hurricane season officially runs from June 1 to November 30, so students should stay alert for many months, not only during one stormy week.

passages.label: Chart
passages.text: 2026 Atlantic outlook: below-normal season 55%; near-normal season 35%; above-normal season 10%. Expected ranges: 8-14 named storms, 3-6 hurricanes, 1-3 major hurricanes.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Passage A?
options: Kevin used hurricane-season information to help make a school safety poster.
Kevin decided to travel during every storm.
The science club canceled all summer activities.
The teacher said storms never cause real problems.
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on Kevin reading the outlook and turning it into a safety poster.

questions.question: When does the Atlantic hurricane season officially run?
questions.explanation: Passage A states that the season officially runs from June 1 to November 30.

questions.question: According to the chart, what is the expected range for named storms?
questions.explanation: The chart says the expected range is 8-14 named storms.

questions.question: Why did Kevin's teacher still want students to prepare for emergencies?
options: Because even one strong storm can still be dangerous.
Because NOAA said storms would never end.
Because the club wanted to sell flashlights.
Because school would stay closed for six months.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that below-normal does not mean there is no danger.

questions.question: What does "outlook" most likely mean in this passage?
questions.explanation: NOAA's outlook refers to its seasonal forecast.

questions.question: What does "it" refer to in "it officially runs from June 1 to November 30"?
questions.explanation: "It" refers to the Atlantic hurricane season.

questions.question: Which statement is supported by both the passage and the chart?
options: Students should not assume a quieter season means zero risk.
The season has a 55% chance of being above-normal.
questions.explanation: The chart shows only probabilities, and the passage explains why people should still prepare.

questions.question: Which season outcome is most likely in the chart? Brief answer: Give one reason Kevin still included emergency tips.
questions.sample_brief_answer: He still included them because a single strong storm can cause serious damage even in a below-normal season.
questions.explanation: The chart gives below-normal the highest probability, and Passage A explains the safety reason.

items.title: A New Champion at Bee Week
items.topic: 拼字比賽、校外學習、多文本整合
items.source: Scripps National Spelling Bee homepage; https://spellingbee.com/; accessed 2026-06-01
items.usage: 依 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee 官方首頁事實重寫短文與活動資訊，未直接複製原文或外部題目。

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: Mia loves words, so she followed the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee online. She learned that Shrey Parikh, a 14-year-old student from San Bernardino, California, became the new champion. He won after a spell-off and correctly spelled 32 words there, setting a new record for that round. Mia was surprised by the winning word, "bromocriptine," because she had never seen it before. Instead of feeling discouraged, she wrote the word in her notebook and decided to learn a few new word roots each week. She said the contest reminded her that strong spelling is not only about memory, but also about staying calm under pressure.

passages.label: Passage B
passages.text: Bee Week Notes: 247 spellers came to Washington, D.C., from across the country and around the world. The 2026 event was held at a new venue, DAR Constitution Hall.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Passage A?
options: Mia followed the spelling bee and felt inspired by the new champion.
Mia decided to stop learning difficult words.
The bee was canceled before the final round.
All students already knew the winning word.
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on Mia learning about the champion and feeling motivated.

questions.question: How old was Shrey Parikh in the passage?
questions.explanation: Passage A says Shrey Parikh was 14 years old.

questions.question: Why did Mia write the winning word in her notebook?
options: She wanted to keep learning from the contest.
She planned to erase it later as a joke.
She had to return it to the judges.
She did not understand who won.
questions.explanation: Her action shows she wanted to study and improve.

questions.question: What does "discouraged" most likely mean in Passage A?
questions.explanation: "Discouraged" means feeling less confident or disappointed.

questions.question: What does "He" refer to in "He won after a spell-off"?
questions.explanation: "He" refers to Shrey Parikh.

questions.question: What does the sentence "strong spelling is not only about memory, but also about staying calm under pressure" mean?
options: Success in spelling also depends on self-control during stress.
Only memory matters in every competition.
Contestants should speak very fast to win.
The judges cared only about handwriting.
questions.explanation: The sentence explains that calm thinking is important, not just memorization.

questions.question: Which statement is supported by both passages?
options: The 2026 spelling bee was a large event with an important final result.
The contest took place in San Bernardino, California.
Only students from one country joined the bee.
The champion won without a spell-off.
questions.explanation: Passage A describes the championship result, and Passage B shows the event was large and international.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 2026 event? Brief answer: Why did the contest motivate Mia?
questions.sample_brief_answer: It motivated her because she saw that difficult words can be learned step by step with practice and calm thinking.
questions.explanation: Passage B gives the host city, and Passage A explains Mia's reaction.

items.title: Watching an Asteroid Carefully
items.topic: 太空科學、風險判讀、多文本整合
items.source: NASA Science article on asteroid 2024 YR4; https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/planetary-defense/2026/03/05/new-nasa-asteroid-observations-eliminate-chance-of-2032-lunar-impact/; accessed 2026-06-01
items.usage: 依 NASA 對 2024 YR4 的最新觀測結果重寫科普短文與時間線，用於事實查證與題材設計，未直接複製原文。

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: During science class, Ms. Huang showed students a short update about asteroid 2024 YR4. New observations from the James Webb Space Telescope helped NASA refine the asteroid's path. The new data showed that the asteroid is expected to pass the Moon on December 22, 2032, at a distance of about 13,200 miles. NASA also said the object poses no significant risk to Earth. Ms. Huang told the class that this was a good example of how science works: experts make early estimates, collect more evidence, and improve their answers. The students agreed that the most important lesson was not to panic when a first report sounds uncertain.

passages.label: Passage B
passages.text: Timeline Note: Early 2025 reports said 2024 YR4 had a small but notable chance of hitting Earth. By March 2026, after more observations, NASA ruled out a lunar impact and said the asteroid no longer posed a significant Earth threat.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Passage A?
options: New observations helped scientists better understand an asteroid's path.
Students discovered a new asteroid by themselves.
NASA warned people to leave Earth at once.
The Moon changed its orbit suddenly.
questions.explanation: The passage is about better data leading to a clearer understanding of the asteroid.

questions.question: About how far from the Moon is 2024 YR4 expected to pass in 2032?
questions.explanation: Passage A gives the distance as about 13,200 miles.

questions.question: Why did Ms. Huang say students should not panic about the first report?
options: Because early reports can change when scientists get more evidence.
Because NASA never studies space objects carefully.
Because the class was not interested in science.
questions.explanation: The passage says science improves answers with more evidence.

questions.question: What does "refine" most likely mean in Passage A?
questions.explanation: NASA refined the path by making its prediction more exact.

questions.question: What does "this" refer to in "this was a good example of how science works"?
options: the process of improving predictions with more evidence
questions.explanation: "This" refers to the process Ms. Huang just described.

questions.question: What does the sentence "experts make early estimates, collect more evidence, and improve their answers" mean?
options: Scientific conclusions can become more accurate over time.
Answers should stay the same even if facts change.
questions.explanation: The sentence explains that science becomes more accurate as new data arrives.

questions.question: Which statement matches both passages?
options: Later observations reduced the earlier concern about 2024 YR4.
The asteroid is now expected to hit Earth in 2032.
Students were told to ignore new evidence.
questions.explanation: Both passages explain that later data lowered the risk.

questions.question: Which tool helped provide the new observations? Brief answer: What bigger lesson did Ms. Huang want students to learn?
questions.sample_brief_answer: She wanted them to learn that scientific answers improve when new evidence is collected.
questions.explanation: Passage A names the telescope, and the lesson is explained directly.

items.title: Rabat and the Year of Books
items.topic: 閱讀推廣、國際文化、段落排序
items.source: UNESCO World Book Capital announcement; https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/unesco-names-rabat-world-book-capital-2026?hub=66703; accessed 2026-06-01
items.usage: 依 UNESCO 對 Rabat 成為 2026 世界圖書之都的公告重寫閱讀推廣短文，保留關鍵事實，不直接複製原文。

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: In reading class, Ms. Chen told students that Rabat, Morocco, was chosen as UNESCO's World Book Capital for 2026. She explained that the city was recognized for supporting reading, helping women and young people through literacy, and fighting illiteracy in underserved communities. Rabat also has 54 publishing houses and one of Africa's large international book fairs. Ms. Chen asked students to imagine what their own town could do if it wanted to celebrate books for a whole year. Some students suggested book exchanges, reading corners, and family storytelling nights. They liked the idea that books could be used not only for study, but also for community change.

passages.label: Passage B
passages.text: Event Note: UNESCO said the year of celebrations for Rabat starts on April 23, 2026, World Book and Copyright Day.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Passage A?
options: Students learned why Rabat was recognized for promoting books and reading.
Students planned to move to Morocco immediately.
UNESCO decided to stop supporting literacy.
Books were removed from the classroom.
questions.explanation: The passage explains Rabat's recognition and the students' response.

questions.question: How many publishing houses does Rabat have according to the passage?
questions.explanation: Passage A states that Rabat has 54 publishing houses.

questions.question: Why did Ms. Chen ask students to imagine ideas for their own town?
options: She wanted them to connect the news to their own community.
She wanted them to forget the passage quickly.
She planned to test their map skills only.
She wanted them to stop reading books.
questions.explanation: Her question helps students apply the idea to real life.

questions.question: What does "underserved" most likely mean in this passage?
questions.explanation: "Underserved communities" are communities that do not receive enough support.

questions.question: What does "They" refer to in "They liked the idea that books could be used..."?
questions.explanation: "They" refers to the students.

questions.question: What does the sentence "books could be used not only for study, but also for community change" mean?
options: Books can support learning and also help improve society.
Books should only be used in tests.
Communities should replace books with screens.
Reading has no connection to daily life.
questions.explanation: The sentence says books can help both individuals and communities.

questions.question: Which order best matches the information in the passages?
options: Rabat is chosen by UNESCO. → Students discuss why the city matters. → They suggest local reading ideas. → The celebration year starts on April 23, 2026.
Students suggest local reading ideas. → Rabat is chosen by UNESCO. → The celebration year starts on April 23, 2026. → The city stops promoting literacy.
The celebration year starts on April 23, 2026. → Rabat is chosen by UNESCO. → Students leave class. → UNESCO closes all book fairs.
Rabat is chosen by UNESCO. → The city removes publishing houses. → Students stop reading. → The celebration year ends before it starts.
questions.explanation: This order follows the passage: recognition first, discussion next, local ideas after that, and the event note gives the start date.

questions.question: On what date does the celebration year start? Brief answer: Name one reading activity the students suggested.
questions.sample_brief_answer: One possible answer is a book exchange, a reading corner, or a family storytelling night.
questions.explanation: Passage B gives the date, and Passage A lists student ideas.

items.title: Roman Telescope Ready for Its Next View
items.topic: 太空探索、工程進度、圖表閱讀
items.source: NASA Roman Space Telescope update; https://www.nasa.gov/missions/roman-space-telescope/nasas-roman-space-telescope-primary-mirror-gets-last-look/; accessed 2026-06-01
items.usage: 依 NASA 對 Roman 太空望遠鏡主鏡最終檢查的更新重寫短文與流程表，保留里程碑事實，不直接複製原文。

passages.label: Passage A
passages.text: Ella read a space article about NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Engineers completed a final inspection of the telescope's primary mirror at Goddard Space Flight Center on May 20 and 21. The mirror is 7.9 feet wide and helps collect and focus light from faraway objects. After this milestone, the team plans to ship the observatory to Kennedy Space Center in Florida in the coming weeks. Ella liked the idea that a long space mission depends on careful small checks first. She wrote in her journal that big discoveries often begin with quiet, patient engineering work.

passages.label: Checklist
passages.text: Mission steps: 1. Final mirror inspection completed. 2. Observatory ships to Kennedy Space Center. 3. Launch preparations continue. 4. Roman begins sending back space views several months after launch.

questions.question: What is Passage A mainly about?
options: A telescope passed an important inspection before the next mission steps.
Ella built a telescope in one day.
NASA canceled all work on the Roman mission.
The mirror was used to study oceans on Earth.
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on the completed inspection and what comes next.

questions.question: How wide is the primary mirror mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: Passage A says the mirror is 7.9 feet wide.

questions.question: According to the checklist, what happens right after the final mirror inspection?
options: The observatory ships to Kennedy Space Center.
Roman begins sending back space views immediately.
The mirror returns to the classroom.
questions.explanation: Step 2 in the checklist is shipping the observatory to Kennedy Space Center.

questions.question: Why did Ella write that big discoveries begin with patient engineering work?
options: She understood that careful preparation is necessary before space science can happen.
She thought engineering was easier than reading.
She wanted NASA to skip testing.
She believed discoveries happen by accident only.
questions.explanation: Her comment shows she understood the value of careful preparation.

questions.question: What does "milestone" most likely mean in Passage A?
questions.explanation: "Milestone" means an important stage in a process.

questions.question: What does "it" refer to in "Ella liked the idea that it depends on careful small checks first"?
questions.explanation: "It" refers to the long space mission.

questions.question: What does the sentence "big discoveries often begin with quiet, patient engineering work" mean?
options: Important science results usually require careful preparation first.
Only loud teams do useful work.
Engineering and science have no connection.
questions.explanation: The sentence explains that careful engineering supports future discoveries.

questions.question: Where will the observatory be shipped next? Brief answer: Why is the final inspection important?
questions.sample_brief_answer: The inspection is important because engineers must confirm the mirror is ready before launch preparations continue.
questions.explanation: Passage A names the next location and explains why the check matters.
